title: MCP Is Not Good Yet — David Cramer, Sentry
talk_summary: David Cramer of Sentry describes building Sentry's remote MCP server and argues MCP is just a pluggable architecture for agents, not a thin wrapper over OpenAPI. His core practical lessons are to hand-design tool responses and errors as agent-facing context (markdown, minimal, human-readable), and to prefer owning an agent you control over exposing raw API endpoints as tools.

takeaways.technique: Design tool outputs as agent-facing context, not raw API JSON
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of proxying OpenAPI endpoints as tools, they intentionally translate responses to minimal markdown with only the essentials a human (and thus the model) can reason about.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we return markdown... I'm just going to give you the bare essentials... if a human can reason about it, the language model can reason about it

takeaways.technique: Design tool errors as first-class context
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat error messages as context for the model, writing human-readable errors that tell the agent what was wrong and how to correct the call, rather than raw machine errors.
takeaways.evidence_quote: errors. Same thing. You got to design the errors. They are still context... give it a real human response

takeaways.technique: Expose agents, not raw APIs, as the integration surface
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than exposing every API endpoint as a tool, they wrap a high-quality agent (root-cause analysis) behind the interface, accepting the cost of that agent in exchange for controlling prompt, model, and result shaping.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I just get a lot more control if I pick up the cost of that agent. I control the model even

takeaways.technique: Constrain tool description and response size deliberately
takeaways.what_they_do: They note token limits on tool descriptions and that returning everything inflates cost per call, so they keep tool descriptions and payloads tight and iterate weekly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that tool call that could have been a dollar might be $10 now because of the amount of tokens you needed

takeaways.technique: Do not allow untrusted MCP tools/packages
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly warn against pulling random MCP tools or packages into an organization, trusting only vetted sources.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Do not allow random MCP tools in your organization. Um, trust people that have earned trust. Don't download random packages off the internet
